text: Photocatalytic degradation of Rhodamine B (RhB) over graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) was investigated under simulated solar irradiation.
The g-C3N4 powder was synthesized by thermal polycondensation of urea at 550 °C for 4 h. The BET specific surface area was 12 m2/g.
In a typical run, 50 mL of RhB solution with an initial concentration C0 of 10 mg/L was mixed with the catalyst at a dosage of 0.5 g/L. A 300 W xenon lamp was used as the light source.

The degradation efficiency, defined as eta = (C0 - Ct) / C0, was monitored by measuring the absorbance at 554 nm on a UV-Vis spectrophotometer (Shimadzu UV-2600) after 30 min of dark adsorption equilibrium. RhB was degraded 96% within 90 min of irradiation.
The same g-C3N4 catalyst was applied to Rhodamine B (RhB) removal under visible light, but the kinetics rather than the endpoint efficiency were the focus of this study.
Experiments were carried out with an initial RhB concentration of 15 mg/L and a catalyst dosage of 1 g/L under a 300 W xenon lamp with a 420 nm cutoff filter.
The degradation followed pseudo-first-order kinetics according to ln(C0/Ct) = kt, giving a rate constant k = 0.031 min⁻¹ over the first 60 min of irradiation (R² = 0.98).
A follow-up study revisited the g-C3N4 / Rhodamine B system and reported removal performance as a dimensionless fraction instead of a percentage.
The RhB initial concentration was 10 mg/L and the catalyst dosage was 500 mg/L, irradiated with a 150 W LED source. The removal efficiency reached 0.92 after 120 min of reaction.
The fraction removed, 1 - Ct/C0, was obtained from absorbance readings at 554 nm on the same UV-Vis instrument as in the earlier work.
